facts: **One application** uses two parallel offsets $d_f$ and $d_l$ separated by strip width $h$: $A \approx \dfrac{h}{2}(d_f + d_l)$.
**Two applications** divide the shape into two strips of width $h$ using three offsets ($d_f$, $d_m$, $d_l$): $A \approx \dfrac{h}{2}(d_f + d_m) + \dfrac{h}{2}(d_m + d_l)$.
The rule **underestimates** area when the boundary curves outward, and **overestimates** area when the boundary curves inward.

Using **more applications** with smaller strip widths $h$ usually gives a closer approximation by following the curved boundary more closely, but this is not guaranteed for every boundary; additional measurements alone do not establish which estimate is closer to the true area.
steps: Identify the strip width $h$ and the lengths of the parallel offsets.
Calculate the area of each trapezium using $\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$.
Sum the trapezium areas to estimate the total area.

workedExamples.solution_text:
a. One application uses the full baseline width.

$\begin{align*} A &\approx \frac{27}{2}(20.8+29.2)\\ &\approx 675\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$

b. Each strip has width $h=27\div2=13.5\text{ m}$.

$\begin{align*} A &\approx A_1+A_2\\ &\approx \frac{13.5}{2}(20.8+27.2)+\frac{13.5}{2}(27.2+29.2)\\ &\approx 324+380.7\\ &\approx 704.7\text{ m}^2 \end{align*}$

To the nearest square metre, the two-application estimate is $705\text{ m}^2$.

foundation.solution_text:

$h = 10\text{ m}$, $d_f = 14\text{ m}$, $d_l = 22\text{ m}$.

foundation.question_text: Use one application of the trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of a riverbank reserve with parallel offset boundaries of $20\text{ m}$ and $32\text{ m}$ separated by a width of $14\text{ m}$.

foundation.solution_text:
1. **Identify the strip width $h$ and the lengths of the parallel offsets.**
$h = 8\text{ m}$, $d_f = 12\text{ m}$, $d_m = 17\text{ m}$, $d_l = 19\text{ m}$.
2. **Calculate the area of each trapezium using $\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$.**
$A_1 \approx \frac{8}{2}(12 + 17) = 4 \times 29 = 116\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{8}{2}(17 + 19) = 4 \times 36 = 144\text{ m}^2$
3. **Sum the trapezium areas to estimate the total area.**
$A \approx A_1 + A_2$
$= 116 + 144$
$= 260\text{ m}^2$

foundation.question_text: Estimate the area of a lake frontage using two applications of the trapezoidal rule, with two equal strip widths of $h = 12\text{ m}$ and offset measurements of $22\text{ m}$, $28\text{ m}$, and $30\text{ m}$.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Identify the strip width $h$ and the lengths of the parallel offsets.**
$h = 12\text{ m}$, $d_f = 22\text{ m}$, $d_m = 28\text{ m}$, $d_l = 30\text{ m}$.
2. **Calculate the area of each trapezium using $\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$.**
$A_1 \approx \frac{12}{2}(22 + 28) = 6 \times 50 = 300\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{12}{2}(28 + 30) = 6 \times 58 = 348\text{ m}^2$
3. **Sum the trapezium areas to estimate the total area.**
$A \approx A_1 + A_2$
$= 300 + 348$
$= 648\text{ m}^2$

The straight dotted line representing the top of the trapezium lies entirely below the outward-curving boundary.
This leaves out the region between the straight chord and the curve.
Therefore, the trapezoidal rule gives an **underestimate** of the true area.

Estimate the surface area of a water channel with $h = 15\text{ m}$, $d_f = 16.4\text{ m}$, and $d_l = 21.6\text{ m}$ using one application of the trapezoidal rule.

development.solution_text:
1. **Identify the strip width $h$ and the lengths of the parallel offsets.**
$h = 15\text{ m}$, $d_f = 26\text{ m}$, $d_m = 34\text{ m}$, $d_l = 38\text{ m}$.
2. **Calculate the area of each trapezium using $\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$.**
$A_1 \approx \frac{15}{2}(26 + 34) = 7.5 \times 60 = 450\text{ m}^2$

development.question_text: A parcel of land with a curved boundary is divided into two strips of equal width $h = 11\text{ m}$. The three perpendicular offsets, in order, are $17\text{ m}$, $23\text{ m}$, and $29\text{ m}$. Estimate the area using two applications of the trapezoidal rule.
development.solution_text:
1. **Identify the strip width $h$ and the lengths of the parallel offsets.**
$h = 11\text{ m}$, $d_f = 17\text{ m}$, $d_m = 23\text{ m}$, $d_l = 29\text{ m}$.
2. **Calculate the area of each trapezium using $\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$.**
$A_1 \approx \frac{11}{2}(17 + 23) = 5.5 \times 40 = 220\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{11}{2}(23 + 29) = 5.5 \times 52 = 286\text{ m}^2$
3. **Sum the trapezium areas to estimate the total area.**
$A \approx 220 + 286 = 506\text{ m}^2$

development.question_text:
A curved boundary over a total width of $40\text{ m}$ has offsets $d_f = 18\text{ m}$, $d_m = 28\text{ m}$, and $d_l = 22\text{ m}$.
Calculate the area estimate using:
a. One application ($h = 40\text{ m}$)
b. Two applications ($h = 20\text{ m}$)
development.solution_text:
One application:
$A \approx \frac{40}{2}(18 + 22)$
$= 20 \times 40$
$= 800\text{ m}^2$
Two applications:
$A_1 \approx \frac{20}{2}(18 + 28) = 10 \times 46 = 460\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{20}{2}(28 + 22) = 10 \times 50 = 500\text{ m}^2$
$A \approx 460 + 500 = 960\text{ m}^2$

development.question_text: Estimate the area of a decorative lake using two applications of the trapezoidal rule. The two equal strip widths are $h = 13\text{ m}$ and the perpendicular offsets, in order, are $19\text{ m}$, $25\text{ m}$, and $23\text{ m}$.
development.solution_text:
1. **Identify the strip width $h$ and the lengths of the parallel offsets.**
$h = 13\text{ m}$, $d_f = 19\text{ m}$, $d_m = 25\text{ m}$, $d_l = 23\text{ m}$.
2. **Calculate the area of each trapezium using $\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$.**
$A_1 \approx \frac{13}{2}(19 + 25) = 6.5 \times 44 = 286\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{13}{2}(25 + 23) = 6.5 \times 48 = 312\text{ m}^2$
3. **Sum the trapezium areas to estimate the total area.**
$A \approx 286 + 312 = 598\text{ m}^2$

development.question_text: A stormwater retention pond has a curved boundary. Three perpendicular offsets, in order, measure $21\text{ m}$, $29\text{ m}$, and $25\text{ m}$, with $11\text{ m}$ between consecutive offsets. Estimate its area using two applications of the trapezoidal rule.

A canal cross-section has a curved boundary and three parallel offsets of $5\text{ m}$, $8\text{ m}$, and $10\text{ m}$, in order. The perpendicular distance between consecutive offsets is $7\text{ m}$. Estimate the cross-sectional area to the nearest square metre using two applications of the trapezoidal rule.
development.solution_text:
1. **Identify the strip width $h$ and the lengths of the parallel offsets.**
$h = 7\text{ m}$, $d_f = 5\text{ m}$, $d_m = 8\text{ m}$, $d_l = 10\text{ m}$.
2. **Calculate the area of each trapezium using $\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$.**
$A_1 \approx \frac{7}{2}(5 + 8) = 45.5\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{7}{2}(8 + 10) = 63\text{ m}^2$
3. **Sum the trapezium areas to estimate the total area.**
$A \approx 45.5 + 63 = 108.5\text{ m}^2$
To the nearest square metre, the estimated area is $109\text{ m}^2$.

mastery.question_text: An irrigation reservoir has a curved boundary. Three perpendicular offsets, in order, measure $37.4\text{ m}$, $49.2\text{ m}$, and $45.6\text{ m}$. The perpendicular distance between consecutive offsets is $23\text{ m}$. Estimate the area to the nearest square metre using two applications of the trapezoidal rule.
mastery.solution_text:
$A_1 \approx \frac{23}{2}(37.4 + 49.2) = 11.5 \times 86.6 = 995.9\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{23}{2}(49.2 + 45.6) = 11.5 \times 94.8 = 1090.2\text{ m}^2$
$A \approx 995.9 + 1090.2 = 2086.1\text{ m}^2$
To the nearest square metre, the estimated area is $2086\text{ m}^2$.

mastery.question_text:
A wetland boundary curves inward (concave up) over the first strip of width $h = 16\text{ m}$ (offsets $30\text{ m}$ to $18\text{ m}$) and curves outward (concave down) over the second strip of width $h = 16\text{ m}$ (offsets $18\text{ m}$ to $28\text{ m}$).
Calculate the total estimated area, and determine for each strip whether the trapezoidal rule overestimates or underestimates that strip's actual area.
mastery.solution_text:
$A_1 \approx \frac{16}{2}(30 + 18) = 8 \times 48 = 384\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{16}{2}(18 + 28) = 8 \times 46 = 368\text{ m}^2$
$A_{\text{total}} \approx 384 + 368 = 752\text{ m}^2$
Strip 1 (curves inward): chord is above the curve, so the rule **overestimates**.
Strip 2 (curves outward): chord is below the curve, so the rule **underestimates**.

mastery.question_text: A lake has a curved boundary with three perpendicular offsets, in order, of $21.6\text{ m}$, $32.4\text{ m}$, and $31.8\text{ m}$. The total perpendicular distance from the first offset to the last is $31\text{ m}$, and the middle offset is halfway between them. Estimate the area to the nearest square metre using two applications of the trapezoidal rule.
mastery.solution_text:
$h = \frac{31}{2} = 15.5\text{ m}$
$A_1 \approx \frac{15.5}{2}(21.6 + 32.4) = 7.75 \times 54 = 418.5\text{ m}^2$
$A_2 \approx \frac{15.5}{2}(32.4 + 31.8) = 7.75 \times 64.2 = 497.55\text{ m}^2$
$A \approx 418.5 + 497.55 = 916.05\text{ m}^2$
To the nearest square metre, the estimated area is $916\text{ m}^2$.
